clue.text: Employment situation's hard in Midlands town

indicators.note: the hard letter is placed in the middle of the town's name, which surrounds it

parts.note: Worksop is a town in Nottinghamshire, in the English Midlands
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A report on jobs in a tough Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: WORKSOP is a small market town in Nottinghamshire; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop is a room or building where people are employed at manual work.

clue.text: Gate that always has a keeper

definitions.meaning: an old word for a small gate or door set in a larger one
the cricket stumps, behind which a wicketkeeper always stands

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielder behind the stumps is the keeper, so the second reading names the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small door or gate, and in cricket the wicket always has a wicketkeeper behind it.

clue.text: Call for record

definitions.meaning: to register a sale on a cash till

explanation.definitionFit: To ring up is to telephone, and a shop assistant rings up a sale by recording it on the till.

clue.text: With this result, crowds are content, possibly

definitions.text: With this result, crowds are content, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the two words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A football result that leaves supporters of both sides satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CROWDS ARE. A score draw is a drawn football match in which both teams score, so both sets of fans go home content.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn match with goals on both sides is the outcome that pleases both sets of supporters.

clue.text: Group loyalty revealed by link with 15

parts.note: the answer to 15 down is a Latin term for the school or college one once attended, one's old school
a tie is a bond or link between people

explanation.surface: Loyalty within a group shown by connection with a former university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed by' and 'with' are links. In Britain the old school tie is literally the necktie in a former school's colours, and figuratively the network of favours among its old pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands for the mutual favouritism and loyalty among former pupils of the same school.

clue.text: State investing nothing in fourth scheme

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the scheme wraps round the zero

parts.note: after plans A, B and C comes plan D
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A government putting no money into its fourth plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' looks financial but means enclosing: PLAN D wraps O.
explanation.definitionFit: Poland is a sovereign country, a nation-state in central Europe.

clue.text: Volunteer not available to serve king

parts.note: a dish that is off can no longer be served in a restaurant
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Someone who offers to help but can't attend to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is usually the Queen, but it also abbreviates Edward Rex, a king.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to put it forward willingly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: From the start of Romans

parts.note: looks like the opening of the Epistle to the Romans, but means a phrase in the Romans' own language for 'from the beginning'

explanation.surface: Reading the Epistle to the Romans from its opening verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Romans' tells you the phrase is Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means from the beginning, the very outset.

clue.text: Lower classes very eager to be included in my political agitation

parts.note: D and E are the lowest social grades in British market-research classification

indicators.note: says the eager word goes inside the word my

parts.note: taken as written
agog means very eager or excited

explanation.surface: The poor are keen to join a political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: British social grades run A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so D and E are the lower classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Demagogy is stirring up popular feeling with emotive appeals, a kind of rabble-rousing politics.

clue.text: Modern craft that has its place in Paris

definitions.meaning: the supersonic airliner of the late twentieth century

definitions.text: that has its place in Paris
definitions.meaning: the name of the large square in Paris, the Place de la ...

explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-French supersonic airliner shares its name with a famous Paris square.

clue.text: Maintain a fine business

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Keep a good company going.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert it firmly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Ride drunk needs to avoid

parts.note: merry is a mild word for tipsy
to go round an obstacle is to avoid it

explanation.surface: A drunkard has to dodge something on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a fairground ride on which people circle on wooden horses.

clue.text: English duet composed after French piece of music

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of duet are arranged anew

explanation.surface: An English duet written after a French piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like the act of writing music, but here it signals a rearrangement. 'after' is a link, and the stray quote mark is an OCR blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a study names a short instrumental composition built to practise a technique.

clue.text: Moth wife found in open area in forest

indicators.note: the wife's letter is discovered sitting within the forest gap

parts.note: a clearing is a treeless space in woodland

explanation.surface: A moth and a wife discovered in a woodland glade.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearwings are day-flying moths with largely transparent wings.

clue.text: Professional from university town checking text

parts.note: pro is short for professional
of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
Reading is an English town with a university

explanation.surface: A professional from a university town checking a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreading is reading copy to find and mark errors before printing.

clue.text: Mother contributed to change in university once

indicators.note: the mother is added into the middle of the word for change

parts.note: to alter is to change
mama is a childish word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother helped bring about reform at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One's alma mater is the university or school one formerly attended.

clue.text: Potter joining one club after another, endlessly

indicators.note: says the last letter of the first golf club is dropped

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club
a wood is another golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer adding one club after another to the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' and 'after' are links. Josiah Wedgwood was the great eighteenth-century English potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Josiah Wedgwood founded the famous Staffordshire pottery firm.

clue.text: Ask one fellow who's the main deity?

parts.note: to pose a question is to ask it
I is the Roman numeral one
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Questioning a man about which god is supreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'chief' but is the old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea, the main being an old word for the ocean.

clue.text: New metal goal constructed for annual school match

indicators.note: constructed means built up from parts, so these letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A new metal goal built for a yearly school fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eton wall game is a peculiar football game played at Eton College, the English public school, most famously on St Andrew's Day each year.
explanation.definitionFit: The wall game is a traditional yearly fixture at Eton College.

clue.text: By splitting membership fee, it becomes excellent

indicators.note: the word for by breaks the fee word into two parts

parts.note: a sub is a subscription paid to a club
per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: Dividing the club fee makes things splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it becomes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means of the highest quality, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Jolly way to introduce church meeting

indicators.note: the street is introduced into the middle of the word for jolly

parts.note: in British speech jolly means very, as in 'jolly good'
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A cheerful way of opening a church gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective but is the British adverb meaning very.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry meeting is the parish ratepayers' assembly, so the room's name stands for the gathering.

clue.text: Minor fictional public school? Not quite

indicators.note: says the school's name stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Greyfriars is the school of Billy Bunter in Frank Richards's comic stories

explanation.surface: A small made-up boarding school that falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like an adjective for the school, but it is the definition: Franciscans are Friars Minor, called grey friars from their habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Franciscan friars, the Friars Minor, were known as grey friars from their grey habits.

clue.text: Take back most of the idle talk

parts.note: back as in 'to and fro', where fro means back

indicators.note: says the final letter of the word the is dropped

explanation.surface: An instruction to withdraw much of a piece of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is an instruction linking the pieces: FRO for 'back' plus TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth is insubstantial chatter, empty talk of no real content.

clue.text: Computer equipment doctor's given by practice

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
use means practice or custom

explanation.surface: A doctor's surgery supplies some computer kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 's given by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is the hand-held pointing device used with a computer.

clue.text: Casual piece of work producing strange book

parts.note: odd means strange
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Occasional work turning out a peculiar book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd job is a small occasional task done casually.

clue.text: Refer to one of the gospels, perhaps, about one result of division

indicators.note: the two pieces together go round the one

parts.note: to quote a source is to refer to it
I is the Roman numeral one
NT is the New Testament, home of the gospels; 'perhaps' flags the loose fit

explanation.surface: Citing a gospel concerning one outcome of a split.
explanation.walkthrough: QUOTENT wraps I after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the quotient is the number got by dividing one quantity by another.

clue.text: Dirty-looking husband on board pleasure boat

indicators.note: being on board means inside the vessel, so the husband goes within

parts.note: dingy means drab and grimy

explanation.surface: A scruffy husband aboard a small leisure craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small sailing or rowing boat used for recreation.

clue.text: Expertly clothing woman in charming fashion

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the adverb surrounds the name

parts.note: ably means skilfully
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman dressed with skill and charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorably means in a delightful, endearing manner, an adverb synonym.
